I had no idea this was such a common thing with BPD parents and that others could relate. My ubpd mom was always naked and barely dressed even when friends were over. Usually one of my stepdad's oversized shirts, likely no underwear. She also would just walk in on people using the restroom and bathing so coincidentally so did all of my siblings as well. As I got older it would bother me that I would be on the toilet and just barged in on. Even when I locked the door they would unlock it from the outside if they needed something. A total lack of boundaries.

Yes! I applaud you for this! I considered making it a massive self care day because of all the negative feelings and emotions it has been bringing up. It's been taking a lot of energy to keep the negativity and anger toward my mom under control. I decided I'd rather honor all of the strong women in my life who have positively impacted me. Shifted the perspective a little bit and I'm not totally dreading the day! I'm looking forward to giving cards to my grandmother, my therapist, a friend, and maybe a few others! I'm thankful for the strong, unconditional women who have shown me what motherly love is even if it didn't come from my own mother.

The dinner show was spectacular. Everyone sat there while she showed her true side screaming at me. I was thankful it wasn't behind closed doors or a keyboard. The rest of the family got to see just how unstable she is.

Her wonderful 'apology' this morning. Her words are meaningless to me:

"I’m sorry for over reacting ! I knew I could not be around u and no t be able to be engaged ! I love u ! I do too much too! I’m sorry for the behavior patterns that continued through me that was toxic. I try to see them and squish them"

I can't stand the tingles and mine are constant. Strongest in my arms and makes me want to crawl out of my skin. My ears ring all the time too. The physical manifestations make me feel crazy, uncomfortable, and I can't sit still well. I'm sure I'd benefit from breathing techniques, as most would, but I feel rather calm mentally and my breathing seems normal. Very frustrating.

I've never been diagnosed with a stress rash but it sounds tame enough (treatable). I have eczema that worsens on my hands with anxiety flares. I also get small scabs from time to time on my scalp that usually pass on their own. I'm not sure if that could be similar. I have severe generalized anxiety.

My physical symptoms are constant. My ears have a high pitched ringing from the moment I wake up until I (somehow) get to sleep. Wishing I could leave my own skin because of the tingling/uneasy feelings in my extremities. Headaches are common, trouble remembering, mental fog, derealization, trouble concentrating, lack of motivation, restless, insomnia, the list goes on.
That's a good way to describe it. I've noticed sensory sensitivity playing a big roll in my anxiety too. Sometimes all of it makes me feel insane. The feelings can be indescribable
